stem: The cell theory, stating that all plants and animals are made of cells, was put forward mainly by
explanation: Matthias Schleiden (plants, 1838) and Theodor Schwann (animals, 1839) proposed that cells are the basic units of living things. Watson and Crick described DNA structure, and the other two pairs proposed models of the cell membrane.

stem: The idea that new cells arise only from pre-existing cells (omnis cellula e cellula) was added to the cell theory by
explanation: Rudolf Virchow (1855) concluded that cells come only from the division of existing cells, ruling out spontaneous generation of cells. Robert Hooke first named cells in cork, and Robert Brown discovered the nucleus.

stem: An electron microscope can resolve much finer detail than a light microscope because
options: its lenses are made of better glass
electrons have a much shorter wavelength than visible light
explanation: Resolving power improves as the wavelength used becomes shorter, and an electron beam has a wavelength thousands of times shorter than light. Electron microscopes use electromagnetic lenses, not glass, and specimens must be dead and in a vacuum.

stem: The resolution (resolving power) of a microscope is its ability to
options: show two close points as separate
stain cell structures in different colours
explanation: Resolution is the smallest distance at which two points can still be seen as distinct. Making an object look larger is magnification; magnifying without better resolution only gives a bigger blurred image.

stem: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by
explanation: In 1972 Singer and Nicolson described the membrane as a fluid phospholipid bilayer in which proteins float like tiles of a mosaic. Danielli and Davson had earlier proposed a protein-lipid-protein sandwich model.

stem: In the Danielli-Davson (sandwich) model, the cell membrane was described as
options: a lipid bilayer between two continuous layers of protein
globular proteins floating freely within a fluid lipid bilayer
a single layer of cellulose fibres
a protein layer between two lipid layers
explanation: Danielli and Davson pictured a phospholipid bilayer coated on both sides by continuous protein sheets. The idea of proteins scattered in and floating through the bilayer is the later fluid mosaic model, which replaced it.

stem: The middle lamella that cements neighbouring plant cells together is mainly composed of
explanation: The middle lamella forms first, between two daughter cells, and is made of calcium and magnesium pectates that hold the cells together. Cellulose makes up the primary and secondary walls laid down on either side of it, and lignin is added later to some secondary walls.

stem: The cell wall of most bacteria is made mainly of
explanation: Bacterial walls are built from peptidoglycan, chains of sugars cross-linked by short peptides. Cellulose is the main wall material of plants and chitin that of most fungi, so these are the usual mix-ups.

stem: The folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane are called
explanation: Cristae increase the surface area of the inner membrane, which carries the electron transport chain and ATP synthase. Thylakoids and grana belong to chloroplasts, and cisternae are the flattened sacs of the ER and Golgi apparatus.

stem: Which pair of organelles both contain their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes?
explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own small circular DNA and prokaryote-like 70S ribosomes, which supports the endosymbiont idea of their origin. The Golgi, ER, lysosomes and peroxisomes have no DNA of their own.

stem: Ribosomal RNA is synthesised and ribosome subunits are assembled in the
explanation: The nucleolus is the dense region of the nucleus where rRNA genes are transcribed and joined with proteins to make ribosome subunits, which then pass out through nuclear pores. The Golgi apparatus packages proteins but does not make ribosomes.

stem: In liver cells, the smooth endoplasmic reticulum is especially important for
explanation: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes; it makes lipids and steroids and, in liver cells, contains enzymes that detoxify drugs and alcohol. Protein synthesis for export is the job of rough ER, whose surface carries ribosomes.

stem: The organelle that modifies, sorts and packages proteins into secretory vesicles is the
explanation: Proteins from the rough ER enter the Golgi apparatus, where they are modified (for example by adding sugars) and packed into vesicles for secretion or for lysosomes. Mitochondria make ATP and centrioles help form the spindle.

stem: The digestion of a cell's own worn-out organelles (autophagy) is carried out by
explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs of hydrolytic enzymes that fuse with old organelles and digest them. Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes such as catalase that break down hydrogen peroxide, not whole organelles.

stem: The 80S ribosome of a eukaryotic cytoplasm is made of two subunits, which are
explanation: Eukaryotic 80S ribosomes have a 60S large and a 40S small subunit. S values measure sedimentation rate and are not simply added, which is why 60S + 40S gives 80S; 50S and 30S are the subunits of the prokaryotic 70S ribosome.

stem: A cell of the pancreas that secretes large amounts of digestive enzymes would be expected to have a well-developed
options: rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus
smooth endoplasmic reticulum and many lysosomes
explanation: Digestive enzymes are proteins made on ribosomes of the rough ER and then packaged for export by the Golgi apparatus. Smooth ER makes lipids, not proteins, so a secretory protein-making cell is rich in rough ER.

stem: In a chloroplast, the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle take place respectively in the
options: outer membrane and the intermembrane space
explanation: Chlorophyll and the electron carriers are in the thylakoid membranes (stacked as grana), where ATP and NADPH are made. The Calvin cycle enzymes are dissolved in the stroma, which uses that ATP and NADPH to fix CO₂; reversing the two is the common error.

stem: Which structure is present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
explanation: All cells make proteins, so all have ribosomes (70S in prokaryotes, 80S in the eukaryotic cytoplasm). Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, so they have no mitochondria, nuclear envelope or Golgi apparatus.
